title: Public and private keys: who encrypts and who verifies

videos.script: Two keys, and two jobs. People mix them up all the time, so this lesson keeps them apart. {{title}} First job: keeping something secret. Ana wants only Vereda's records service to read a letter. She encrypts with the service's public key. Only its private key opens it. {{encrypt}} Second job: proving who wrote something. Ana signs the letter with her own private key. Anybody with her public key can check the signature. {{sign}} Change one word of the letter, and the check fails. {{tamper}} Notice who holds what. To keep a secret, you use the other side's public key. To sign, you use your own private key. {{grid}} Real systems use both, plus the symmetric cipher of lesson 1, and the last part of the lesson shows how they fit. {{hybrid}}
